Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
Despite service of notice, no one appeared on behalf of the complainant.
2. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.275 of 2023, under Sections 323, 376-D, 506 IPC and Section 5g/6 of POCSO Act, Police Station Patti, District Pratapgarh.
3. In terms of the FIR lodged on 15.07.2023, it was alleged that on 12.07.2023, the applicant along with two accomplice had enticed the daughter of the informant and committed wrong on her.
It was also stated that she informed about the same on 14.05.2023, as such, the FIR was lodged on Priyanshu Gupta vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home, ...

1 15.07.2023,
In the statements under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C., the victim reiterated the same version as contained in the FIR.
The tentative age of the victim is around 15-16 years as per the radiological examination.

4. The Counsel for the applicant draws my attention to the medical examination report, which was done on 15.07.2023, the victim before the medical authority stated that a person known to her along with two unknown person had committed wrong on her.
Subsequently, in the medical examination report, it was observed that the victim was undergoing menstrual cycle bleeding and it was the fifth day of bleeding.
Based upon the same, the Counsel for the applicant argues that the entire prosecution story is stand belied as allegedly on the date of incident, the victim was in menstrual cycle.
5. Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer.

6. Considering the medical examination report, prima facie, the allegations levelled against the applicant are not believable coupled with the fact that the applicant is in custody since 22.07.2023 and the criminal antecedents have been duly explained in the supplementary affidavit filed today,
which is taken on record, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Priyanshu Gupta be released on bail in the aforesaid first information report on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
